name: The Giant Trees of Bambaroo
description:
SUNDAY 29 NOVEMBER. Please note we have had to change the walk from Mt Spec to somewhere away from Paluma due to road closure on the weekend on Mt Spec Rd.

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL - please see details below.
 
WALK DESCRIPTION
Giant Trees Walk - on the Bambaroo Track. We will be climbing up from Bruce Hwy to a higher elevation on Paluma range. The start is a very hot and very steep 1 hr road walk climb and then we reach the rainforest, shade and the giant trees area. The giant strangler fig trees and buttress trees are amazing. After having a look at the many trees we will keep climbing up the range on a forest track. The turn around point will be decided on the day based on the group and we will return via the same route. The plan is to have an early start to beat some of the heat for the steep road walk in first hour.

Type of walk – Very steep track walk up the range - 4 hrs climbing up the range. Tracks have uneven footing including tree roots and rocks.  We will walk out and back via the same route. There is no water resupply en route (there is a creek water point we use near the top of the range, but cannot guarantee water this time of year there). Afternoon is all downhill (apart from one bump)!
   
RATED – Hard to the elevation gained.
    
COST – non-members $5 fee.    
    
WHAT TO BRING 
- Carry drinking water for the walk (carry water for the day 4 lt).
- Lunch, snacks / energy food
- Electrolytes (recommended)
- Sun protection - hat, sunscreen
- Insect repellent
- Enclosed sturdy footwear
- Recommend long sleeve clothing / gaiters to avoid scratches. Some members also wear fingerless gloves
- Hike/Trek pole(s) can be handy on track walks for some.    
    
MEETING POINT – Meet at 0700 at Frosty Mango.   
    
Estimated Completion – back at cars by 5:00 pm (in time for have ice creams at Frosty Mango, a great reward).  
   
Must be over 18yrs to participate.    
  
REGISTRATION
The walk leader is Keith.
Please contact Keith directly if you have his details or email the club at tsvbush@hotmail.com and we'll get back to you asap.
 

Please note:
 To protect the privacy of club officials, walk leaders, property owners or sensitive areas, contact details and some locations won't be published on Facebook or website. Please contact the club via email and we will respond ASAP. 
 
 On some activities, walker numbers may be limited to promote the safety and enjoyment of all, due to location size and ability to socially distance or to reduce our environmental impact at some locations.
 
 Water refill - if you don't like creek refills, then you need to carry water for the day, at least 4 lt, or more to suit your own requirements. The Club recommends that any creek water refills are suitably treated / filtered before consumption.  Drinking creek water is at your own risk and responsibility. 

 COVID-19
 Please do not attend if you are unwell, have symptoms or have been ordered to quarantine or isolate. Social distancing and self managed hygiene practices are strongly encouraged, and the club will not be organising car pooling opportunities at present. The club is cognisant of the QORF COVID SAFE PLAN for Outdoor Recreation Providers. On some walks, as noted above, numbers may be limited.
 
 We hope to see you on a walk soon.

name: Upper Cloudy Creek - Paluma
description:
SUNDAY 22 November

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

RATED: Hard - creek based rock hopping bushwalking


DESCRIPTION
We'll start from Paluma village and traverse down Cloudy Creek to about halfway down the mountain range. That means a steep climb after lunch back to the village (approx 400 mr elevation climb back up the creek). 
There will be steep rock faces (some with exposed ledges), rockhopping, uneven footing, and the potential for slippery rocks. 

FITNESS
To be suitable for this walk, a good analogy would be doing a Castle Hill spur, without a track, three times with ease before lunchtime. You will need to be fit and agile with good balance.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for full day eg minimum 4L (refill from the creek is not recommended on this walk).
- Clothing: long sleeve clothing/gaiters is recommended for sun protection and to protect from scratches. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Swimming gear

COST
Non members = $5 walk fee
Must be over 18years to participate

WALK LEADER, INFO and REGISTRATION
Walk leader is Keith.
To discuss suitability, to register or for more information please contact Keith directly or email tsvbush@hotmail.com and we will get back to you asap. 

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 8:30am at the carpark for Paluma Range National Park McClellands Lookout walking track section - Loop Road. 
Return time: by 4:30pm due to Mt Spec Rd closure at 6pm.

name: Mt Spec area and Diorite Falls
description:
REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. Please see details below.

A rainforest track bushwalk in the Mt Spec area. Highlights will include Diorite Falls, Waterfall Creek, Shay’s Clearing, and will try the DCK ice bath. 
  
Type of walk – 22 km rainforest track walk. May be some minor rock hopping at the creeks. Tracks have uneven footing including  tree roots and rocks. Will be some steep hills along the route. 
  
Rated – MEDIUM HARD  
   
Cost – non-members $5 fee.   
   
What you need – carry drinking water for the walk (minimum 2 lt and refill from creeks, or carry water for the day 4 lt). Lunch,  snacks / energy food, electrolytes, hat, sunscreen, insect repellent, enclosed sturdy footwear. Recommend long sleeve clothing / gaiters to avoid scratches. Some members also wear fingerless gloves. Hike/Trek pole(s) can be handy on track walks for some. Swimming attire for the swims.  
   
Timing and meet – Meet at 0815 at Paluma Dam car park (the outside car park).  
   
Estimated Completion – back at cars by 4:30 pm.  Mt Spec Road closes at 6 pm. 
  
Must be over 18yrs to participate.   
  
Water refill - if you don't like creek refills, then you need to carry water for the day, at least 4 lt, or more to suit your own requirements. The Club recommends that any creek water refills are suitably treated / filtered before consumption.

name: Little Crystal Creek
description:
SUNDAY 1 NOVEMBER - Little Crystal Creek

REGISTRATION WITH THE WALK LEADER IS ESSENTIAL. PLEASE READ THE INFORMATION BELOW.

DESCRIPTION
An off track, creek based walk to explore the lower reaches of Little Crystal Creek. We'll leave from Little Crystal Creek Bridge on Mt Spec Rd and rock hop down the creek to the bottom of the range. There will be some pretty scenery, a ravine and a good waterfall to swim in at the bottom.

The forecast for Rollingstone on Sunday is 33C. There is little shade in the creek and probably no breeze until we get to the bottom (this will make the swim extra nice!).

DIFFICULTY - Medium Hard

FITNESS
It is not a long distance, but reasonable off-track fitness is required for the steep hill climb and rock hopping.

WHAT TO BRING
- Water: you will need water for half day eg minimum 3L or refill from the creek (treating the water is recommended)
- Clothing: there is a lot of long grass and scrub so full long sleeve clothing is recommended. Many members also wear fingerless gloves.
- Enclosed footwear
- Food for the day
- Hat, sunscreen and insect repellent
- Usual bushwalking gear 
- Personal first aid kit including a compression bandage and blister kit is recommended.
- Swimming gear

WALK DETAILS
Meet time: 7:15am at cnr of Barrett Rd (south junction just past Ollera Ck) and Bruce Highway
Return time: aim to be back at the cars by 2pm

Non members = $5 walk fee for insurance

Must be over 18years to participate
